name: 74LV4052PW,118
title: Dual 4-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer
summary: Two single-pole four-throw CMOS switches share one 16-pin package. Each joins its common terminal nZ to one of four channel terminals nY0 to nY3; the select pair S1 and S0 picks the same channel number in both switches, and a HIGH on the active-LOW enable E opens all eight channels. A closed channel carries signal either way, so each half serves as a 4:1 multiplexer or a 1:4 demultiplexer. Logic levels are taken against GND while the signal path sits between VCC and a separate VEE pin, and 3 V logic steers analog signals that swing ±3 V; VCC spans 1.0 V to 6.0 V and the ON resistance peaks at 60 Ω typical on a 4.5 V supply.
key_figures: two SP4T switches; 4:1 multiplexer or 1:4 demultiplexer per switch
separate VEE pin for the analog path
60 Ω typ, 135 Ω max at VCC = 4.5 V; 80 Ω typ, 180 Ω max at VCC = 3.0 V to 3.6 V
36 ns typ, 71 ns max at VCC = 3.0 V to 3.6 V
180 MHz typ at VCC = 3.0 V; 200 MHz typ at VCC = 6.0 V
20 μA max at VCC = 3.6 V to 85 °C
HBM class 2 over 2000 V; CDM class C3 over 1000 V

circuits.title: OFF-state leakage current
circuits.description: E sits at VCC, so every channel is open whatever the select inputs do. One source feeds the common terminal through an ammeter and a second source feeds the channel terminal through another, and each ammeter reads the current that crosses the open channel. One source goes to VCC and the other to VEE, then the two are swapped.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
GND and VEE are tied together for this measurement.

circuits.title: ON-state leakage current
circuits.description: E sits at GND, so the channel the select pair picks conducts. A source holds the common terminal at VCC or VEE while the channel terminal is left open, and an ammeter in that branch reads the current the closed channel passes.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
GND and VEE are tied together for this measurement.

circuits.title: ON resistance
circuits.description: E sits at GND and the select pair closes one channel. A current source pulls ISW out of the common terminal while a source holds the channel terminal, and a voltmeter across the closed channel reads VSW. Sweeping the source over the whole signal range gives RON against input voltage.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
GND and VEE are tied together for this measurement.

circuits.title: Switching times
circuits.description: A pulse generator feeds the part through a termination resistor RT that matches the generator's own impedance, and the waveform at the far terminal is watched across a load of CL to ground, RL to VEE and a second RL to an external supply VEXT. For propagation delay the generator drives a channel terminal and the waveform is read at the common terminal; for enable and disable time it drives E or a select input. VEXT, CL and RL follow the supply.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.

circuits.title: Total harmonic distortion
circuits.description: A sine source drives the common terminal through a 10 μF coupling capacitor with E at GND, so the picked channel conducts. The channel terminal is biased halfway up the supply by two 2RL resistors, loaded by CL, and a distortion meter reads the output.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
RL = 10 kΩ and CL = 50 pF for the distortion figures.

circuits.title: Frequency response
circuits.description: A sine source drives the common terminal through a 0.1 μF coupling capacitor with E at GND. The channel terminal is biased halfway up the supply by two 2RL resistors and loaded by CL, and a dB meter follows the output level as the drive frequency rises.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
RL = 50 Ω and CL = 50 pF for the -3 dB frequency.

circuits.title: Isolation (OFF-state)
circuits.description: The same arrangement as the frequency-response measurement, but with E held at VCC so every channel is open. The dB meter then reads how much of the drive still reaches the loaded channel terminal.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
RL = 600 Ω and CL = 50 pF for the isolation figure.

circuits.title: Crosstalk voltage between digital inputs and switch
circuits.description: A pulse generator drives the select inputs while the common terminal is biased halfway up the supply by two 2RL resistors and E is held at a steady logic level. A voltmeter on the channel terminal, loaded by two more 2RL resistors and CL, catches the step Vct that each logic edge throws into the signal path.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
The pulse may be applied to a select input or to E.
RL = 600 Ω and CL = 50 pF for the crosstalk-voltage figure.

circuits.title: Crosstalk between switches, on channel
circuits.description: A source drives the common terminal through a 0.1 μF capacitor and a series RL, with E at GND so one channel conducts. That channel's terminal carries the signal into a 2RL pair, CL, a voltmeter and a dB meter; the idle channel terminal sits on its own 2RL pair.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
RL = 600 Ω and CL = 50 pF for the crosstalk figure.

circuits.title: Crosstalk between switches, off channel
circuits.description: A source drives the channel terminal that is not selected, which carries a 2RL to VCC and an RL to ground, while E sits at GND and the select pair holds the other channel closed. The common terminal, biased by a 2RL pair and loaded by CL, is watched with a voltmeter and a dB meter.
notes: The measurement holds for any channel of either switch and that switch's common terminal.
RL = 600 Ω and CL = 50 pF for the crosstalk figure.

equations.name: Dynamic power dissipation
equations.expr: PD = CPD × VCC² × fi × N + Σ((CL + Csw) × VCC² × fo)
equations.note: The sum runs over the outputs.

operation.text: S1 and S0 together pick one channel out of four: L L closes nY0 onto nZ, L H closes nY1, H L closes nY2 and H H closes nY3. Both switches follow the same select levels, so the two halves always carry the same channel number.
E is active LOW. Hold it LOW and the selected channel conducts in each switch; take it HIGH and all eight channels open, whatever the select inputs do.

A closed channel conducts in either direction: nZ can feed one nYn terminal, or any nYn terminal can feed nZ. Each half therefore works as a 4:1 multiplexer or a 1:4 demultiplexer, for analog or digital signals.

VCC runs from 1.0 V to 6.0 V against GND, with 3.3 V as the nominal value, and VEE is a second supply that sets how far below ground a switched signal may reach. The guaranteed operating area spans 1 V to 6 V in both VCC - GND and VCC - VEE, with the two opposite corners of that square trimmed off.
The part translates logic levels: 3 V logic steers analog signals that swing ±3 V.

Both the digital inputs and the switch terminals are specified for 0 V up to VCC. An input edge may be no slower than 500 ns/V while VCC is 1.0 V to 2.0 V, 200 ns/V from 2.0 V to 2.7 V, and 100 ns/V from 2.7 V to 6.0 V.
Clamp diodes sit on E, S0 and S1, so a series resistor that limits the current lets one of them be driven from a source sitting above VCC.
Switching from one channel to another is typically break-before-make.

RON is not flat across the signal range: it reaches a peak somewhere between the rails and falls towards either rail. At VCC = 4.5 V the peak is 60 Ω typical, against 45 Ω at GND and 50 Ω at VCC - VEE, and channel-to-channel mismatch is 3 Ω typical. Near VCC - VEE = 1.2 V the resistance turns strongly non-linear, and on such a supply the part suits digital signals only.

A signal crossing a closed channel is delayed by 5 ns typical at VCC = 3.3 V. Closing a channel from E or a select input takes 36 ns typical and opening it 26 ns typical at that supply into 50 pF; into 15 pF the two fall to 30 ns and 22 ns.
Switching times are taken at a level VM that follows the supply: half of VCC below 2.7 V and above 3.6 V, and a fixed 1.5 V between those two.
A digital input presents 3.5 pF typical. A channel terminal nYn presents 5 pF and the common terminal nZ presents 12 pF.
Static supply current is 20 μA max at VCC = 3.6 V up to 85 °C, and 40 μA up to 125 °C. A digital input held 0.6 V below VCC adds up to 500 μA per input between VCC = 2.7 V and 3.6 V.

The digital inputs meet the JEDEC level standards: JESD8-7 for 1.65 V to 1.95 V, JESD8-5 for 2.3 V to 2.7 V, JESD8C for 2.7 V to 3.6 V and JESD36 for 4.5 V to 5.5 V. They also accept TTL levels while VCC sits between 2.7 V and 3.6 V.
Total dissipation is capped at 500 mW over the whole temperature range. Above 110 °C the SO16 package gives up 12.4 mW/K of that budget, and above 91 °C the TSSOP16 package gives up 8.5 mW/K.
Human body model withstand passes 2000 V, class 2 of ANSI/ESDA/JEDEC JS-001; charged device model passes 1000 V, class C3 of JS-002. Latch-up immunity passes 100 mA to JESD78 class II level B.
